input.rationale: Added a competing-cause control for the now-asserted snapshot-boundary loop. The sealed-partition harness runs the same legal five-node history twice, differing only in how much of its log the successor leader keeps when it snapshots inside the follower's stale suffix: with TrailingLogs=0 the leader's retained log begins above the index the follower's prev-log check needs and the loop occurs; with TrailingLogs=3 the leader keeps the entries below the boundary and the same history converges with no snapshot at all. The control is registered so the controller retains the receipt.

investigations.question: Is the snapshot-boundary loop caused specifically by the leader's compaction leaving its retained log above the index the follower's prev-log check needs, so that the identical history converges when the leader keeps a few trailing entries?

interpretations.rationale: Construction feedback from the sealed-partition harness, run locally with both settings and otherwise identical inputs, separates the cause. TrailingLogs=0: divergent_prefix reports base_index 2, divergence_index 3, partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 1..7; successor_snapshot reports snapshot_index 4 with successor_store 0/0; rejoin_observe reports restores_before 0, restores_early 724, restores_late 734, partner_applied_index 4 pinned at the snapshot index and partner_last_index 7. TrailingLogs=3: the precondition is identical (partner_store 1..7 with earlier-term entries from index 3), the successor's snapshot is at the same index 4 but its store now retains 2..4, and rejoin_observe reports restores_before/early/late all 0 with partner_applied_index 4 and partner_last_index 4 - the follower's stale suffix was replaced by ordinary AppendEntries and no snapshot was needed. So the loop's necessary condition is the leader's retained log starting above the index needed to rebuild the request (which is what sends replicateTo to SEND_SNAP); retaining even a few entries below the boundary lets the leader back the prev-log index down into entries it still holds, and the follower truncates its stale suffix normally. This is recorded as construction feedback only: no measured conclusion is asserted in this batch, and the earlier retained witness (CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30, TrailingLogs=0) and the assertion built on it stand on their own basis.
counterevidence: With TrailingLogs=3 the same history converges with zero snapshot installs, so leader compaction past the boundary is load-bearing and the loop is not a property of the partition, the uncommitted suffix or the snapshot itself.
The default TrailingLogs (10240) would delay but not remove the condition: it is reached once the leader's log extends that far past its snapshot index, which this harness did not sample.
limitations: Source-only in this batch: the two-case harness has not been executed by the controller yet, so the quoted counts are non-retained local runs.
Only trailing values 0 and 3 were compared, at one snapshot index and one configuration; the exact threshold (how many trailing entries suffice) was not characterised.
The harness counts InstallSnapshot installs via the follower FSM's Restore count rather than on the wire, and no RPC-level trace is collected.

scope.description: Five-node legal history per case: {leader, partner} isolated from the other three in both directions, the leader replicating uncommitted commands to the partner only, a successor elected by the majority that commits its entry at the first divergent index and snapshots there under the case's TrailingLogs, then a heal. Observations: the precondition, the successor's snapshot and store bounds, per-node timeline, and the partner's InstallSnapshot count over ~1.5 s.
assumptions: Both cases share the rest of the configuration, so any difference in the partner's outcome is attributable to how much log the successor retains.
Sealing the partition on both sides is required for the partner to be genuinely isolated, as established by the superseded harness.
The partner's FSM Restore count identifies InstallSnapshot installs without touching production logic.
excluded: No RPC-level instrumentation, no network transport, and no default (10240) TrailingLogs sampling.
The threshold at which the loop disappears is not characterised.

experiment.prefix: For trailing in {0,3}: MakeClusterCustom(Peers=5, Bootstrap=true, Conf{TrailingLogs: trailing, SnapshotInterval:1h, SnapshotThreshold:1<<20, HeartbeatTimeout/ElectionTimeout/LeaderLeaseTimeout:1s, CommitTimeout:10ms}, MakeFSMFunc returning a Restore-counting MockFSM). Wait for a leader; partner=followers[0], others=remaining three; disconnect leader<->other and partner<->other in both directions and emit partition; base=leader.LastIndex(); fire five leader.Apply calls; wait until partner.LastIndex()>base and emit divergent_prefix with trailing_logs; wait up to 12 s for a successor among others, apply one command, Snapshot(), emit successor_snapshot with its store bounds; FullyConnect(); emit a per-node timeline at 0/200/400/700/1000/1300 ms with states, indexes, store bounds, entry terms at 3/4/5 and the partner's Restore count; finally emit rejoin_observe with the restore counts, the partner's and successor's indexes and store bounds, and trailing_logs.
experiment.responsibility: The audit must identify which mechanism carries the failure: compaction depth, partition, or the snapshot transfer itself.

investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot but never calls setLastLog nor invalidates the pre-existing log entry at L. getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, so once the snapshot makes lastSnapshotIndex == L while the stale log entry keeps lastLogIndex == L, the tie is resolved in favour of the stale log term. The follower's PrevLogEntry==L check then compares the leader's snapshot term T against the stale term and answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. The leader sets nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1), which lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) then needs the leader's own log entry L-1, which is absent once the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index (compactLogsWithTrailing can leave firstIndex > L-1), so replicateTo jumps to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the same snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
investigations.discriminator: Drive one node with real RPCs: bootstrap it as a Nonvoter, seed a command at index 2 with an AppendEntries whose Term is 2, install an InstallSnapshot with LastLogIndex=2 and LastLogTerm=3, then send AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The necessary property is met only if the last append succeeds; the suspicion holds if it fails while an otherwise identical control node without the seeded entry succeeds. Refuted if the post-snapshot append succeeds in both cases, or if getLastEntry reports the snapshot term for index 2.

gaps.question: Does the leader side actually restore the blocking state in one execution: with a leader whose log has been compacted so that the snapshot index L is at its head, does an unrepairable follower produce repeated InstallSnapshot attempts with no committed progress rather than converging after one snapshot?

investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: Reconfirmed against the retained receipt: the follower keeps the log-derived term for the snapshot index and therefore rejects the leader's boundary AppendEntries; the leader-facing retry cycle remains source-sourced pending its own execution.

gaps.question: Reachability: can one compatible multi-node history legally produce the precondition (a follower holding an earlier-term entry at exactly the index where a later-term leader later commits and snapshots), rather than the harness's single seeded AppendEntries, without the follower's higher term forcing the leader to step down?

investigations.question: With a leader whose retained log begins above its snapshot index L and a follower that keeps advertising an earlier term for L, does one execution show repeated InstallSnapshot attempts and persistent non-progress on that follower, or does the leader converge after one snapshot?
investigations.hypothesis: The follower rejects every AppendEntries whose PrevLogEntry is L (stale term from getLastEntry). The leader computes nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1) = L, then setPreviousLog(L) needs the leader's own entry L-1; because the leader compacted up to its snapshot index, GetLog(L-1) returns ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, sendLatestSnapshot restores nextIndex = L+1, and the next append is rejected again. The cycle restores its own precondition and has no enabled repair, so the leader re-ships the snapshot repeatedly while the follower's applied index stays at L.
investigations.discriminator: Control peer and defect peer share one harness and differ only in whether an earlier-term entry occupies index L: one snapshot and applied index L+1 refute the suspicion; repeated InstallSnapshot calls together with an applied index pinned at L support it.

investigations.question: Does one legal multi-node history, built from real producers rather than a seeded RPC, actually reach the state in which a follower holds an earlier-term entry at the leader's snapshot index and then stays unrepairable, or do ordinary repair paths close the gap before the snapshot boundary is exercised?
investigations.hypothesis: A leader isolated from three of four peers can replicate uncommitted entries to exactly one follower; a successor elected by the remaining three commits its own entry at the first divergent index, snapshots there and compacts past it; on heal the follower should then reject PrevLogEntry at the snapshot index and the leader should fall into the snapshot loop. Local construction feedback did not show this: the follower converged with zero snapshot restores.
investigations.discriminator: Read the rejoin_observe event: restores_early/restores_late above zero with the follower's applied index pinned at the snapshot index supports the loop; restores at zero with the follower's applied index reaching the leader's applied index refutes it for this history.

investigations.question: Does one legal multi-node history, built from real producers rather than a seeded RPC, reach the state in which a follower holds an earlier-term entry at the leader's snapshot index and then stays unrepairable, or do ordinary repair paths close the gap before the snapshot boundary is exercised?

gaps.question: By which path did the diverged peer get reconciled in the executed five-node history, given that the term-3 successor's own log store was empty (first=last=0) so it could not serve entries 3..4, the peer's FSM was never restored, and the peer's final store is 1..4 with applied index 4? Candidate explanations that remain untested include an intervening election or leadership change, repair driven by a different node, and a path through AppendEntries that does not require the successor's log store.

investigations.question: By which path is a diverged peer reconciled when the current leader's own log store has been fully compacted, and which node supplies the entries that replace its stale suffix?

gaps.question: Which node sent the AppendEntries that replaced the peer's stale suffix in the five-node history, and does that path exist only because a different node had already installed the successor's snapshot (which would leave it holding lastLogIndex above lastSnapshotIndex with only the post-snapshot logs retained)?

investigations.question: With a partition that truly seals the leader and one partner from the other three peers, does the legal history still reach the state in which the partner holds earlier-term entries at the successor's snapshot index, and does the partner then stay unrepairable?

scope.description: Two nodes in one process over InmemTransport: 'server-1' under test (Nonvoter so it never campaigns) and 'server-2' as the RPC producer. A control and a defect case run the same two/three RPC steps and differ only in whether an earlier-term leader first stored a command at the snapshot index.
assumptions: The isolated target executes the root package '.' directly; the harness is an in-package test so it may call unexported handlers and state accessors.
InmemTransport with two connected transports suffices because the claims concern one follower's response to a leader's RPCs; only the InmemStore (non-monotonic) is exercised.
BootstrapCluster writes the configuration entry that makes server-1 a Nonvoter, so the node never starts an election and the driven RPCs keep a stable term.
excluded: No net/tcp transport and no multi-node partition history; the leader-side snapshot loop is out of scope for this harness.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap server-1 as a Nonvoter in a configuration whose only Voter is server-2 (BootstrapCluster then NewRaft, so the node starts its own run/runFSM loops). Defect case step 1: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=2, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[{Index:2,Term:2,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=1) so the node stores a term-2 entry at index 2. Step 2: server-2 sends InstallSnapshot(SnapshotVersion=1, Term=3, LastLogIndex=2, LastLogTerm=3, Configuration=<server-1 Nonvoter/server-2 Voter>, ConfigurationIndex=1, Size=len(payload), payload=msgpack-encoded empty [][]byte) which the MockFSM restores. Step 3: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=3, PrevLogEntry=2, PrevLogTerm=3, Entries=[{Index:3,Term:3,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=2). The control repeats steps 2-3 only. Each step emits CA_EVENT JSON with the response and the post-snapshot last_log/last_snapshot/getLastEntry values.
basis.responsibility: installSnapshot and raftState.getLastEntry must leave a single, unchallenged view of the last durable entry: a snapshot supersedes any log entry at the same index.

scope.description: One process, two real Raft instances over InmemTransport. server-A is bootstrapped as a single-voter cluster, becomes leader, applies six commands, then takes a user snapshot with TrailingLogs=0 so its retained log starts above the snapshot index. server-B is bootstrapped as a Nonvoter under the same configuration so it never campaigns, and is seeded with earlier-term (term 1) commands up to the snapshot index (defect) or one index short of it (control) via a legal AppendEntries from a third in-memory transport. server-A and server-B are then connected and server-A is asked to AddVoter(server-B).
assumptions: The isolated target runs the root package '.' directly, so the harness is an in-package test and may wrap the transport to count InstallSnapshot calls.
A single-voter cluster bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster reaches leadership on its own after the election timeout, which keeps the leader-side prefix free of partition machinery.
AddVoter is issued without waiting on its future because the config entry cannot commit while the peer is unrepairable; the observation window starts after a fixed delay.
excluded: No network transport, no partitions, and no more than one peer; leader elections among multiple voters are out of scope.

basis.prefix: server-A: inmem transport wrapped by a counting decorator that increments on every InstallSnapshot call; BootstrapCluster(conf.TrailingLogs=0, config={A:Voter}); NewRaft; wait for Leader; six Apply(new command) calls; Snapshot() and record its Index L and the store's FirstIndex. server-B: separate inmem transport, BootstrapCluster(config={A:Voter,B:Nonvoter}) then NewRaft, so B is a follower that never campaigns; a third inmem transport connected to B sends AppendEntries(Term=1, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[index 2..L term 1]) for the defect sub-case or [index 2..L-1] for the control sub-case. Both sub-cases then connect A and B, call A.AddVoter(B, addrB, 0, 1s) without blocking on the future, sleep 300 ms, read the InstallSnapshot counter, sleep 1200 ms, read it again, and emit CA_EVENT loop_observe with the counter pair, the snapshot index, and the follower's applied and last indexes together with the leader's last and commit indexes.
basis.responsibility: Leader-side replication must make progress for a follower that is behind rather than re-shipping the whole snapshot indefinitely, and a snapshot install must remove the follower-side condition that caused the rejection.

scope.description: Five real Raft instances in one process (MakeClusterCustom, BootstrapCluster, InmemTransport, InmemStore, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=1s). Path: wait for a leader; isolate the leader from the three peers that are neither the leader nor a chosen partner by disconnecting both directions of those links; apply five commands that reach only the partner; wait for election of a successor among the other three; apply one command on the successor so its FSM has something to snapshot; take a user snapshot and record its index L together with the divergence index; heal with FullyConnect; sample the partner's FSM Restore count at 300 ms and 1500 ms and the partner's/leader's applied indexes.
assumptions: The isolated leader keeps leadership long enough to append (LeaderLeaseTimeout=1s equals the heartbeat timeout, satisfying config validation), and the majority side elects a successor in a higher term.
Each node's FSM is a wrapper counting Restore calls, so InstallSnapshot deliveries to the partner are observable without touching production logic.
The follower must be seeded through the real replication path: the leader's own AppendEntries to the partner carry the uncommitted suffix, so the divergent entries have an actual producer.
excluded: No network transport and no process separation; fault injection is limited to link disconnection and healing.
The snapshot-boundary loop itself is not re-derived here; this harness only asks whether the precondition is reachable from a legal history.

basis.prefix: MakeClusterCustom(Peers=5, Bootstrap=true, Conf{TrailingLogs:0, SnapshotInterval:1h, SnapshotThreshold:1<<20, HeartbeatTimeout/ElectionTimeout/LeaderLeaseTimeout: 1s, CommitTimeout:10ms}, MakeFSMFunc returning a Restore-counting MockFSM). Wait for a leader and four followers; pick followers[0] as the partner and the three remaining nodes as others; for each other, disconnect the leader transport from it and its transport from the leader, leaving leader<->partner connected. Record base=leader.LastIndex(), fire five leader.Apply commands without waiting, and wait until partner.LastIndex() > base. interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader side (replication.go 223, 256, 286-300, 370): nextIndex becomes L via max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); setPreviousLog(L) requires the leader's entry L-1; once the leader has compacted past L (compactLogsWithTrailing can set firstIndex > L-1) that lookup returns ErrLogNotFound, which routes to SEND_SNAP and re-installs the same snapshot. Local construction feedback (harness assurance_generated_test.go, both sub-cases, run in a scratch copy) matched the prediction exactly: with the stale same-index entry, state_after_snapshot reported last_log_index=2/last_log_term=2 against last_snapshot_index=2/last_snapshot_term=3 and the follow-up append returned success=false/no_retry_backoff=true; without the seeded entry the same append returned success=true. That run is not a retained receipt, so the defect claim is left unresolved pending the controller's execution of the registered experiment; the leader-side loop of the gap above is likewise still unexecuted.
counterevidence: Behind-follower case does not trigger it: when the follower's lastLogIndex is below the snapshot index, getLastEntry returns the snapshot pair and the appended entries are accepted (observed as the harness control: last_log_index=1 < last_snapshot_index=2 -> success=true).

With the default TrailingLogs the leader normally retains entries below its snapshot index, so setPreviousLog(L) succeeds, the leader backs off one index and appendEntries truncates the conflicting suffix from its stored copy, converging without a snapshot loop; the loop needs the leader to have compacted up to or past L.
